# Bouncing Off Walls

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Bouncing Off Walls

In Chapter 3 you did basic wall bouncing. But there was a small problem hiding in that code.

When you check if (x < 0) you are checking the center of the ball. But the ball has a radius. Its edge reaches the wall before its center does. That means the ball clips into the wall before bouncing. It looks slightly off and the player notices even if they cannot explain why.

The fix is simple. Check the edge of the ball, not the center.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3const radius = 10;
4let x = 200, y = 150;
5let dx = 2, dy = 1.5;
6function update()  {
7    x += dx;
8    y += dy;
9    if (x - radius < 0 || x + radius > canvas.width) dx = -dx;
10    if (y - radius < 0 || y + radius > canvas.height) dy = -dy;
11}
12function draw()  {
13    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
14    ctx.beginPath();
15    ctx.arc(x, y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
16    ctx.fill();
17}
18function gameLoop()  {
19    update();
20    draw();
21    requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);
22}
23gameLoop();
```

Click Run Code and you will see the ball bouncing cleanly off every wall without clipping.

Here, x - radius < 0 checks whether the ball's left edge has crossed the left wall, and x + radius > canvas.width checks whether the right edge has crossed the right wall. Both conditions are checked in one if - hitting either wall flips dx. The pattern is the same for dy.

```javascriptDOM
if (x - radius < 0 || x + radius > canvas.width) dx = -dx; 
if (y - radius < 0 || y + radius > canvas.height) dy = -dy;
```

It is the kind of detail that separates a game that feels right from one that feels slightly off. The player's eye notices when the ball clips into walls even if they cannot articulate why. Spending one extra line on radius-aware checks is always worth it.

In Brick Breaker, the bottom wall is the exception — reaching y + radius > canvas.height ends the game instead of bouncing. You will handle that in the Brick Breaker project.
